rationale: Three-lens review (blind, edge-case, acceptance) found one confirmed real bug: AssistantCloneEventBase declared Field(index=True) on assistant_id/user_id alongside identically-named explicit Index() entries, producing a duplicate-name collision in __table__.indexes (verified at runtime: 5 index objects, 3 unique names before fix). Fixed by dropping the redundant index=True. Verified post-fix: 3/3 unique names. Full test suite (56 tests across model/repository/router/service) passes after the fix. Remaining findings are either deliberate, spec-documented decisions (no access validation on source_assistant_id, no anti-abuse throttling — both explicitly called out in spec.md's Design decision and Known limitation sections and confirmed with the user during brainstorming) or pre-existing patterns shared with the sibling update_reaction_counts/increment_usage_count methods (the read-then-write race on the cached count column), not regressions introduced by this diff. Acceptance lens confirmed all spec architecture points implemented; the two divergences it flagged (update_clone_count return-type/not-found behavior, AssistantListResponse default) both match the codebase's actual established convention rather than the spec's prose, which was corrected during planning (see plan.md Self-Review Notes) — not defects.

business_review.evidence: assistant.py:687 clone_count: Optional[int] = SQLField(default=0, index=False); migration adds nullable Integer column with server_default='0'.

assistant.py:577 clone_count: Optional[int] = None — matches the existing unique_likes_count/unique_dislikes_count convention on this same response model (both also default None, not 0); AssistantBase (the persisted side) does default to 0 per spec.

business_review.evidence: assistant_clone_event.py; verified via unit test test_assistant_clone_event_table_args_have_no_unique_constraint and runtime index-name check.

assistant_clone_event_repository.py; unit tests confirm repeat calls from same user both logged.

assistant_repository.py:299-323, structurally identical to update_reaction_counts (fetch fresh row, set field, save, return); returns the original assistant object on not-found rather than None as spec prose stated — but this exactly matches update_reaction_counts' and increment_usage_count's own established not-found behavior, so the implementation is more consistent with the codebase than the spec text was. Documented as a deliberate correction in plan.md.

business_review.evidence: assistant.py:755-770; integration test confirms an exception during clone tracking does not fail assistant creation.

No throttling logic present; spec.md's Known Limitation section explicitly defers this to a follow-up ticket.

standards_review.notes: All 9 commits use 'EPMCDME-10889: <description>' format consistent with recent repo history.
No blocking violations found; new code follows existing sibling patterns (assistant_user_interaction.py, assistant_user_interaction_repository.py) for structure and docstrings.

No secrets, injection, or auth-bypass issues found. source_assistant_id lack of access-check is a deliberate, spec-documented soft-metric tradeoff, not a security gap in the sense of exposing protected data — no data is read or returned based on the unvalidated id, only a counter write is attempted.
